cards.title: Who was assigned no offer?
cards.original: Fifteen percent of students without mentoring withdrew in their first year.
cards.rewrite: Of the 610 baseline respondents assigned no mentoring offer, 93 had a recorded withdrawal before transfer by month 12 and 7 outcomes were unknown. Among the 603 with a known outcome, 93 withdrew.
cards.next: Plan permitted registry follow-up through month 12 and document which outcomes still cannot be observed.

cards.title: Which students does the percentage represent?
cards.original: About fifteen percent of first-year students at these colleges withdraw.
cards.rewrite: In the 1,600-person Tonmick invitation roster, 257 withdrawals before transfer by month 12 were recorded and 11 outcomes were unknown. Holding the known labels fixed, the roster withdrawal fraction ranges from 16.06% to 16.75%.
cards.next: Compare a defined all-enrollee roster with the invitation list and measure withdrawal coverage among those left out.

cards.title: What did the offer change?
cards.original: Mentoring reduced withdrawal by about two percentage points.
cards.rewrite: Under the stated assignment and outcome assumptions, the conservative 95% design interval for the effect of a mentoring offer on withdrawal before transfer by month 12 is −16.15 to +11.45 percentage points in the randomized cohort.
cards.next: Plan a new blocked offer study with more colleges and more complete permitted outcome follow-up, sized for a predeclared worthwhile reduction.

cards.title: What did the service count capture?
cards.rewrite: For archived support visits, the adjusted Poisson offer rate ratio was 1.135 at common covariates and recorded enrollment time. The working 95% intervals were 0.990 to 1.300 with row-level robust uncertainty and 1.005 to 1.281 with the approximate college-grouped calculation.
cards.next: Use a fixed follow-up window and identical recording across services in a study of the offer’s effect on cumulative use.

cards.title: Are those scores or underlying states?
cards.original: Stress and wellbeing are moderately related (r = −.36).
cards.rewrite: Among 922 Tonmick baseline respondents with both five-item scores complete, the recorded stress and wellbeing scores had a Pearson correlation of −0.363.
cards.next: Collect a second measure for each construct at the same baseline occasion and examine whether shared measurement errors could account for the observed association.

bindings.R10_SENTENCE: Among 922 Tonmick baseline respondents with both five-item scores complete, the recorded stress and wellbeing scores had a Pearson correlation of −0.363.

cards.title: Where did the forecast work?
cards.original: A model built from entry records identifies students at risk of withdrawal.
cards.rewrite: On 100,000 later simulated Tonmick records under no mentoring offer, the frozen enrollment forecast had a Brier score of 0.1377 versus 0.1489 for the fixed development comparator. Its AUC was 0.689 for withdrawal before transfer by month 12.
cards.next: Before rollout at a new college, score the frozen rule and comparator on matched later outcomes and check calibration where the office plans to act.
